---

The first framework designed to build and experiment with graph-based intrusion detection systems using deep learning architectures, on two kinds of data: host provenance (processes, files and netflows of each host), for provenance-based intrusion detection systems (PIDSs), and network events (authentications and flows between hosts), for network intrusion detection systems (NIDSs).
It provides a single codebase and a single pipeline to run most recent state-of-the-art systems of both families, on the datasets of both, and easily customize them to develop new variants.

 Release notes

 Version Date Highlights 
 --------- ------ ------------ 
 Unreleased ( main ) Network intrusion detection: Euler, Argus, Jbeil, LARES, E-GraphSAGE and Anomal-E, LANL and OpTC network flow datasets, systems of both families on network or provenance datasets. Faster, leaner pipeline with identical results (Orthrus on THEIA E5: 3.4 h → 61 min, 370 → 16.6 GB peak RAM; graphs 5x smaller on disk). Tests in CI on a sample of CLEARSCOPE E3. Runs on macOS (Apple Silicon, Docker Desktop on CPU) for most datasets, ideally with 32 GB of RAM 
 4.0.0 Nov 2026 Unified tokenization ( featurization.tokenization , renamed tokenizer arguments), configurable graph cleaning ( construction.cleaning ), fixed queue, time-window and node-time-window evaluations, MAGIC kNN fix 
 3.0.0 Oct 2026 Pretrained encoders (SPIDER, CyberGFM, language models, self-supervised GNNs) as node featurization for any PIDS, stable optim to reduce instability, upgrade many packages including torch 1.13.1 (CUDA 11.7) = 2.1.2 (CUDA 12.1) 
 2.2.0 Jul 2026 Interactive 3D embedding viewer, ThreaTrace ground truth 
 2.1.1 May 2026 State of the repo for the KDD'26 paper, improved Velox 
 2.1.0 Apr 2026 Carbanak v2 and Atlas v2 datasets, dataset download script, Docker and W&B fixes 
 2.0.0 Jan 2026 FIVEDIRECTIONS and TRACE datasets, tuned hyperparameters, simplified pipeline stages (renamed arguments) 
 1.0.1 Oct 2025 Deterministic graph construction and word2vec, REAPr labels, Apptainer installation, dataset preprocessing scripts 
 1.0.0 Jun 2025 Initial release, with 8 PIDSs and the DARPA TC and OpTC datasets 

See the releases for the full notes.

 Pretrained Encoders

Any provenance-based system can replace its node featurization (e.g. word2vec ) by an encoder pretrained on provenance data.

 Encoder Description 
 --------- ------------- 
 SPIDER (NeurIPS 2026) transformer entity encoder distilled from a GNN teacher, with pretrained weights 
 CyberGFM BERT pretrained on random walks, then fine-tuned as a detector 
 GPT-2, Llama 3.2, OPT General-purpose language models fine-tuned on entity labels 
 BERT, RoBERTa, ModernBERT, LogBERT, Llama Language models trained from scratch on random walks 
 GraphMAE, GAE, DGI, DeepWalk, node2vec Self-supervised GNNs and walk embeddings 

See the documentation to download the weights, pretrain an encoder and fine-tune it as a detector.

 📄 Documentation

A comprehensive documentation is available, explaining all possible arguments and providing examples on how integrating new systems.

 Pipeline

The framework integrates a pipeline composed of seven stages, shared by provenance and network systems, each parameterizable via configurable arguments, enabling flexible customization of new systems.

install.title: Setup
install.html:
⬇️ Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/ubc-provenance/PIDSMaker.git
💻 Installation with Docker

We have made the installation of PIDSMaker including pre-processed databases for the provenance datasets (DARPA TC, OpTC, ATLASv2, CARBANAKv2) easy and fast. Simply follow these guidelines. The network datasets are built from the files of LARES for now.

PIDSMaker runs on Linux with or without an NVIDIA GPU, and on macOS (Apple Silicon) with Docker Desktop on CPU, for most datasets: a laptop with 32 GB of RAM is ideal. The largest datasets (TRACE_E3 and the E5 datasets) need a server.

usage.title: Basic usage of the framework
usage.html:
Once you have a followed the installation guidelines, you can open a shell in the pids container and experiment in multiple ways. Replace SYSTEM by a provenance system (velox, orthrus, nodlink, threatrace, kairos, rcaid, flash, magic, ocrapt) or a network system (euler, argus, jbeil, lares, egraphsage, anomal_e), and DATASET by a provenance (e.g. CADETS_E3) or network (LANL, OPTC_NET) dataset.

  1. Run in the shell:

    python pidsmaker/main.py SYSTEM DATASET

  2. Run in the shell, monitored to weights & biases (W&B):

    python pidsmaker/main.py SYSTEM DATASET --wandb

  3. Run in background, monitored to W&B (recommended for multiple parallel runs and for research):

    ./run.sh SYSTEM DATASET

You can still watch the logs in your shell using tail -f nohup.out.

To run in the foreground without W&B, with the same settings as ./run.sh, use ./run_local.sh SYSTEM DATASET.

We generally using using W&B for experiment monitoring and historization (see installation guidelines).

Warning: Before performing evaluations, you should tune all systems (see docs here).
